title: Pluggable extraction/classification/merge endpoint (OpenAI-compatible local chat) → fully-local harvesting
priority_note: The BIGGEST egress for private data is extraction — turning a doc into articles sends its full content to Anthropic, whose endpoint is hardcoded. Local embeddings (US-39.2) don't help if extraction still ships the whole document to the cloud. This makes the extraction/classification/merge provider pluggable so harvesting can run against a local OpenAI-compatible chat model.

background.reference: lib/loopctl/llm/anthropic.ex:37 @base_url "https://api.anthropic.com/v1" (hardcoded); the extraction/classification/merge models are per-tenant (tenant_llm_settings.ex: extraction_model/classification_model/merge_model) but the ENDPOINT + provider shape (Anthropic messages API) are fixed. Local chat servers (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp) speak the OpenAI /chat/completions shape, not Anthropic's.
background.includes: Two viable approaches: (a) add an OpenAI-compatible chat provider selectable via config (a sibling to the Anthropic client behind a provider behaviour), keyed by a per-tenant/deployment extraction_base_url + provider type; or (b) if using a local server that emulates Anthropic's API, just make the Anthropic base_url configurable. Approach (a) is more general (most local servers are OpenAI-shaped). Default stays Anthropic. This is more work than US-39.2 because it's a different API shape, not just a base_url.

story.i_want_to: run the extraction/classification/merge LLM steps against a local OpenAI-compatible chat model
story.so_that: a private document's full content is processed entirely on my own infrastructure and never sent to Anthropic (or any third party)

rationale: Closing the embedding leak without closing the extraction leak leaves the larger exposure open. Abstracting the extraction provider behind a behaviour (Anthropic default + an OpenAI-compatible local option, selected by config) lets the whole harvest pipeline run local, completing true data sovereignty when combined with US-39.1/39.2.

acceptance_criteria.description: The extraction/classification/merge LLM call is resolved through a provider behaviour with at least two implementations: the existing Anthropic client (default) and an OpenAI-compatible chat client. Selection is config-driven (per-tenant and/or deployment: an llm_provider + extraction_base_url). Default config = Anthropic, byte-identical to today (regression test).

When configured for the local/OpenAI-compatible provider with a local extraction_base_url, an end-to-end harvest (ingest → extract → article) completes with NO call to api.anthropic.com (mock asserts zero). Token-usage accounting, circuit-breaker, and retry behavior work for the local provider path too (reuse US-37.1/37.3 admission + breaker).

Set via the existing config surface (set_llm_config MCP tool / PATCH), cached + bust like other settings; agent-discoverable via the tool docstring. Validation: http(s) URL; unreachable/misconfigured endpoint degrades via the existing provider-error path, not a crash. No UI.

Output-shape parity: the extraction result (article/knowledge structure) is normalized so downstream (novelty gate, linking, storage) is provider-agnostic. A test compares the parsed extraction output shape across providers for a fixed input (deterministic stubs).

test_cases.name: default remains Anthropic
expected_results: Anthropic client; existing extraction tests pass unchanged

test_cases.name: local provider harvest, no Anthropic egress
expected_results: local stub called; api.anthropic.com never contacted; article produced

test_cases.name: provider-agnostic output shape
steps: extract the same input via each

technical_notes: Files: new lib/loopctl/llm/provider.ex behaviour + lib/loopctl/llm/openai_compatible.ex impl (sibling to anthropic.ex), the extraction/classification/merge call sites (route through the behaviour), tenant_llm_settings.ex (llm_provider enum + extraction_base_url), set_llm_config controller/OpenAPI + MCP tool, config/runtime.exs deployment defaults.

OpenAI /chat/completions vs Anthropic /messages differ in request/response shape + system-prompt handling — the OpenAI-compatible impl adapts both directions. Keep the prompt templates provider-neutral where possible.
Reuse the epic-37 Provider.Admission gate + circuit breaker for the new provider path (don't bypass admission).
Bigger than US-39.2 (new API shape, not just base_url) — consider scoping to extraction-only first, classification/merge as follow-on if needed.
MCP-server change → package.json bump. Config-based DI; no Application.put_env in tests.
